members.note: FText here, like UMG's -- a rich text block is prose, not a field's value.

A data ASSET mapping tag to style rather than a UDataTable of RichTextStyleRow, which is the same job in this library's own shape. Its sibling ImageData answers <img=key/>, which UMG spells as a decorator.

The extension point for markup here is a pair of DATA ASSETS, not a list of subclasses: ImageData answers <img=key/> exactly as UMG's built-in image decorator answers one from its brush table, and CustomStyleData answers <MyTag>. Both are authored properties with setters that re-parse, which is the whole of what a decorator list buys in UMG.

FDreamRichTextStyle IS the inline default style: colour, size, and now the outline/shadow/glow struct. Which of it is in effect is EDreamUIStyleSource plus the per-field bOverride_ bits, rather than one bOverrideDefaultStyle flag.
Pushed onto the paragraph, which is what a content-sized parent measures: a rich text block IS its paragraph, stretched to the control's rect.

The same question with three answers instead of two: the project sheet, this instance, or the sheet with this instance's ticked fields written over it. Lives on UDreamUIControl, shared by every control in the family.
EDreamUITextTransformPolicy -- the library's own None/ToLower/ToUpper. The authored string is untouched; only the drawing changes.
EDreamUITextOverflowType, which has UMG's two answers (Truncate is Clip, Ellipsis is Ellipsis) plus the two that decide whether a long line wraps. SetTextOverflowPolicy carries the UMG name.
Appearance lives in the style struct, so the colour moves through SetStyle or the project sheet. A second setter writing the inline struct would be silently inert whenever StyleSource is the sheet.
A drop shadow here is the UNDERLAY, carried by FDreamRichTextStyle::TextStyle. Alpha zero means no shadow, which is the shipped default and therefore what every existing block draws.
In em rather than pixels, so the shadow reads the same at every font size.

A font DATA ASSET rather than an FSlateFontInfo: the size is Style.FontSize and the outline is Style.TextStyle. SetDefaultFont/GetDefaultFont read and write Style.Font, and markup may still switch the face per run -- this is what a run that says nothing gets. Null leaves the paragraph on the font it has.
A strike-through here is drawn by the text renderer from UDreamText::bStrikethrough, not composited from a replaceable Slate brush. There is no image in that path for a brush to be.
Off by default, the paragraph's own default. It only bites under the overflow types that do not already wrap -- VerticalOverflow always does.
Forwards to SetOverflowType; one writer, two spellings.
The whole default look at once, which is what a style struct is.
Null keeps the library's own text material, which is what every existing block uses.
Going back to the sheet is what clearing the overrides means here: SetStyleSource(ProjectStyleSheet). Per-field clearing is the bOverride_ bits on the struct.

Instances over the style's material and pushes it onto the paragraph; asked twice, the same instance comes back. Null when the style names no material -- an instance of the library's shared text material would let one caller edit every paragraph in the project.

Replacing what the markup resolves against, which is what SetDecorators does in UMG. SetCustomStyleData is the same road for tag styles. Both re-parse, because which tag means what is read while parsing and not afterwards.
Re-parses on the way in, which is what the markup costs.
Re-parses, because which tag means what is read while parsing and not afterwards.

There is no decorator object to return. FRichTextParser evaluates every tag directly against the two data assets and hands the result to the text renderer; nothing in that path is an object a caller could be given, hold on to, or reconfigure. Extension here is done by authoring a data asset, not by subclassing a decorator.
Pushes the same prose through the parser again, which is what picks up a style or image asset edited in place since the last parse.
